title: Qi Kingdom
capsule: The Qi Kingdom (岐國) was a short-lived regime established by the warlord Li Maozhen, who from his base at Fengxiang in the Wei River valley had defied the late Tang court and controlled a bloc of prefectures in the Guanzhong and Longyou regions. In 907, when Zhu Wen abolished the Tang and proclaimed the Later Liang, Li Maozhen refused submission and declared a formal state; however his realm was hemmed in by the Later Liang to the east and the expanding Former Shu to the south and west. By 924 Li Maozhen submitted to the Later Tang emperor Li Cunxu, ceding his territories and ending the last autonomous successor power in the northwest.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The prefectural extent of Li Maozhen's territory is reconstructable from Chinese dynastic histories (Zizhi Tongjian), though precise boundaries between his authority and adjacent warlord domains are not always specified.
